scenarios.name: Job visibility
scenarios.expected: Website HTTP GET /recruitment/jobs/:id and the persisted RecruitmentJob row (the same row WhatsApp's menu service and iOS's identical HTTP path both read) report the same id and status.

scenarios.name: Candidate ingestion
scenarios.expected: HTTP search (website/iOS) and WhatsApp's direct RecruitmentCandidateQueryService.query() call return the identical candidate id, job id and ATS score (90.0) for the same seeded candidate.
scenarios.actual: Both paths returned matchScore=90, same candidateId and jobId.

scenarios.name: Score boundary (>80 vs >=80)
scenarios.expected: scoreGreaterThan excludes the exact-80.00 candidate; scoreGreaterThanOrEqual includes it. Both operators return identical id sets on the HTTP path and WhatsApp's direct call.
scenarios.actual: scoreGreaterThan=80 returned 4 ids, excluding the exact-80.00 candidates. scoreGreaterThanOrEqual=80 returned 6 ids, including both exact-80.00 candidates. Identical id sets on both call paths in both cases.

scenarios.name: Location filtering (Noida / Delhi NCR region)
scenarios.expected: City and region filters return identical id sets across both call paths; the Delhi NCR region taxonomy expansion is a strict superset of the single-city Noida result.
scenarios.actual: 26 ids for city=Noida; 48 ids for region=Delhi NCR (superset confirmed, includes Gurugram etc.). Identical id sets on both call paths for each filter.

scenarios.name: Combined filters
scenarios.expected: score + region + skills + experience applied together return the identical id set on both call paths.
scenarios.actual: 3 ids returned, identical on both call paths.

scenarios.name: Sorting determinism
scenarios.expected: score_desc is a true non-increasing sequence; the two exact-80.00 ties break deterministically by ascending application id, per RecruitmentCandidateQueryService.buildOrdering's documented secondary sort key.
scenarios.actual: Sequence was non-increasing throughout; the two tied candidates appeared adjacent, in ascending-id order (positions 4 and 5 of the page).

scenarios.name: Pagination correctness
scenarios.expected: Walking all pages with a 20-row page size yields no duplicate ids and the full totalCount; a filter change on a fresh request (no stale cursor) returns exactly the new filtered set.
scenarios.actual: 6 pages walked, 120 distinct ids, totalCount=120 (exact match, no duplicates, no gaps). The filter-changed request returned exactly the 6 expected score>=80 ids with no contamination from the prior cursor's position.

scenarios.name: Human review state propagation
scenarios.expected: A recruiterDecision change via POST /recruitment/applications/:id/review is visible, identically, via both the HTTP search path and WhatsApp's direct query call, with no per-client cache to go stale.
scenarios.actual: Both paths returned recruiterDecision=SHORTLISTED immediately after the review call. Website UI also confirmed via a real page reload.

scenarios.name: Export consistency at scale
scenarios.expected: Exported row count (CSV and XLSX) equals the live filtered total, exceeding the query service's 100-row page size — re-verifying the Phase 3 truncation-bug fix from Phase 4's independent cross-platform lens.
scenarios.actual: liveTotalCount=120, csvRowCount=120, xlsxRowCount=120 — exact match for both formats.

scenarios.name: Authorization and revocation
scenarios.expected: resolveAuthorizedUser (the gate every inbound WhatsApp message passes through) resolves before revocation and returns null after; website JWT auth is unaffected by the WhatsApp-specific revocation; a cross-tenant jobId filter exposes zero candidates.
scenarios.actual: Resolved to the correct org/user/link before revocation; returned null immediately after revokeLink(). Website search still worked identically post-revocation. Cross-tenant search for the same jobId returned totalCount=0.
